title: Tail-aware throughput surface probe for queue-pressure in mixed-session continuous-batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a specialized load-test harness that maps throughput (tokens/sec) against queue pressure and tail latency for mixed-session workloads under the continuous-batching runtime. This ticket focuses on building an experiment matrix and the automation to run repeatable sweeps that vary: concurrency mix, session length distribution, arrival burstiness, and KV-cache-hit ratios. Goal: characterize the performance surface, identify load regions where queueing amplifies p95, and produce regression detection alerts keyed to model variant and kernel selection heuristics.
motivation: Existing benchmarks exercise homogeneous arrivals or single-session-length mixes and miss emergent tail amplification when long and short sessions co-exist. Services in the wild show p95 regressions when short interactive sessions are interleaved with long streaming sessions; we need actionable telemetry that ties those regressions to batching/queueing behavior so runtime routing and batching heuristics can be improved.
hypothesis: When a small proportion (~5-15%) of long-token sessions is present in a high-concurrency short-session workload, continuous batching increases aggregate tokens/sec up to a point but creates queue pressure that disproportionately increases p95 for short sessions. We expect a non-linear region in the throughput-vs-queue curve where p95 rises >2x despite only modest throughput gains.
experiment_plan: Implement workload generator that can synthesize session mixes: short (avg 30 tokens), medium (200 tokens), long (2000 tokens)
Parameterize arrival process: Poisson baseline, bursty Pareto tails, and stratified bursts simulating traffic spikes
Sweep concurrency from 50 to 2000 sessions; vary long-session fraction from 0% to 20%
Toggle KV cache hit rates (0%, 50%, 90%) to emulate personalization/streaming reuse
Run each config for 30 minutes with warmup period and collect per-session timing and token counters
Repeat experiments across 3 hardware profiles and two model variants (int8 quantized and float16)
run_configuration: Harness runs orchestrated by bench-runner v0.9 with reproducible seeds
Telemetry exported to bench-dash (Prometheus + perf-collector) with 1s granularity
Duration: 30m test + 10m warmup + 10m cool-down per config
Artifact retention: logs and traces stored in s3://redwood-bench/artifacts/ENG-33147/
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness can run complete sweep without manual intervention and produce a result bundle
Bench dashboard shows throughput vs queue-length surface and p95 heatmap for each model/hardware pair
Regression detector produces a baseline from control runs and flags deviations >20% p95 with classification tags (queue-pressure, kernel-change, kv-miss)
Runbook entry created describing how to interpret the surface and recommended runtime mitigations (batch cap, short-session prioritization)
preliminary_results: Initial runs on hw-medium with 10% long sessions show the predicted non-linear region: tokens/sec increased by ~18% between low and medium queue length regions, but short-session p95 increased from 120ms to 320ms (2.7x). Batch size histograms show opportunistic growth to 32 requests per batch during bursts; kernel-switch events correlate with p95 spikes. KV cache disabled runs reduce p95 amplification, suggesting cache eviction and lock contention are amplifiers.
next_steps: Extend the sweep to include adaptive-priority scheduling enabled in the runtime and compare surfaces
Add synthetic tenant isolation runs to see multi-tenant cross-talk effects
Open an RFC with runtime team proposing short-session fast-path heuristics and a limit on batch growth during detected high-tail conditions
Create a follow-up ticket to integrate regression detector alerts with CI and PR gating
